newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Erwin clarifies competition policy process.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Erwin clarifies competition policy process.

text.p: Trade and Industry Minister Alec Erwin on Tuesday dismissed speculation that he planned to appoint a task group to draft new competition policy.

He told a media briefing that a "discussion agenda" on new competition policy would be sent to the National Economic Development and Labour Council (Nedlac) this month and that it would have three months to discuss it.
His department would then draft new legislation, which would then go through the normal parliamentary process.

"I will reserve the right to consult exactly who I like and I will consult quite widely...so the kind of hype (about task teams and who would be on them) is just a complete misconception," Erwin said.

"The key issue that we stress is that there is clearly a distinction between competition policy, which is a matter which can be affected by a wide range of legislation and the competition law which is a body to achieve certain things and you can't achieve everything with the law.
"So we are looking at a wider reform."
He announced that Cape Town lawyer Christine Qunta and Robin McGregor had been appointed to the Competition Board and further appointments would be made shortly.

Erwin said his department was also trying to improve the capacity of the business practices committee, which had been asked to in particular investigate the complexity of contracts between small businesses and government.
